Keysight's quarter ended 2026-07-31 produced revenue of 1.85 billion, net income of 397 million, a gross margin of 65.87 percent and a net margin of 21.51 percent, and the segment detail shows total segment operating income of 613 million [D1]. The Communications Solutions Group contributed 1.35 billion of revenue and 458 million of operating income, and the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group contributed 501 million of revenue and 155 million of operating income [D1]. Total assets stand at 11.92 billion, shareholders equity at 6.57 billion and net debt at 141 million [D1]. Orders of 2.09 billion were 56 percent above the prior year, and management guided the fourth quarter to revenue of 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion and earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 [D1]. The shares closed at 333.42 in an uptrend, above the 20-day average of 330.47 and the 200-day average of 289.31, with a forward price to earnings of 20.66 against a trailing price to earnings of 45.89 and trailing earnings per share of 7.38 [D2][D7].

The market is arguing about whether demand or supply is the binding constraint on the next few quarters, because management said supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue, called the supply environment less flexible than a year ago and said conversion of demand into revenue is likely to be nonlinear [D3]. Against that, management said demand is far exceeding its ability to supply, that the pipeline continues to grow strongly and that it expects orders slightly up from the third quarter, with another record quarter above 2 billion [D3]. The news coverage reads the same quarter as a record, with orders up 56 percent to 2.09 billion and fourth-quarter guidance well above consensus [D2]. The bull side also leans on the valuation gap between a forward price to earnings of 20.66 and a trailing price to earnings of 45.89 [D7], while the bear side points to management's caution that one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 will not repeat, which raises the bar for the comparison ahead [D3], and to the observation that analyst price targets are often overly optimistic and rarely indicate where a share price is actually heading [D7].

The plan is therefore to hold into the next report rather than add, and to let the supply commentary and the margin comparisons settle the argument [D3]. Confirmation of the bull case would be fourth-quarter revenue inside the guided 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion range and orders above 2 billion for a third consecutive quarter [D1][D3]. Confirmation of the bear case would be revenue at or below the 1.85 billion of the quarter ended 2026-07-31, or a gross margin below 65.87 percent, or a net margin below 21.51 percent [D1]. On the chart, the close of 333.42 sits just above the immediate support high edge of 332.78 and well below immediate resistance at 366.41, so the plan treats 332.78 as the level whose loss would mark a break in the uptrend [D2].

Before the next results, management speaks at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference on September 11, 2026 and at the 2026 Truist Technology Symposium on September 15, 2026, which gives the plan two dated checkpoints on supply and orders [D6].
